commits.subject: Fix Spring Rabbit advice scope access under indy isolation

diagnoses.analysis: This is the required-status aggregate, not an independent test failure. Its workflow depends on test-latest-deps and exits 1 when that dependency fails. Both failed latest-dependency shards have the same PR-introduced private-field access bug fixed by the candidate commit; no workflow change or rerun request is warranted.

Spring Integration/Rabbit cooperation and AMQP handoff tests fail because Spring Rabbit ExecuteListenerAdvice cannot access AdviceScope.request or AdviceScope.previousRequest after indy helper isolation. Java 17 compilation emits nestmate private-field accesses, but the enclosing instrumentation nest host is not available in that loader. Enter fails after opening a processing scope and exit also fails, causing missing completed traces and context leaks. The candidate gives only those two fields package access, preserving the existing lifecycle. The complete non-broker AMQP handoff suite passes with baseline and frozen latest dependencies.

diagnoses.analysis: The Spring Rabbit latest-dependency test shard hits the same two IllegalAccessErrors introduced by the scoped-request change. The resulting unfinished processing spans explain missing metrics, trace timeouts and after-class advice failures. The candidate removes private visibility only from the two fields accessed by ExecuteListenerAdvice, so no missing nest host is needed. Installed-agent registration/template tests, all processing unit tests, Spring-disabled tests and Checkstyle pass for both baseline and latest dependencies; latest bytecode is confirmed to be Java 17 with package-access fields.

metadata.body:
Producer-packed batches delivered to an ordinary `MessageListener` were counted as one message. Count logical deliveries within the Spring processing span so `messaging.client.consumed.messages` and `messaging.batch.message_count` reflect delivered fragments, including when a failure prevents delivery of the remaining batch.

- **Accounting:** Count fragment dispatches rather than trusting producer count headers; retain single-message and list-batch behavior.
- **Ownership:** Preserve producer correlation, error handling, context cleanup, and Spring/RabbitMQ processing ownership. Leave `consumerBatchEnabled` unchanged.
- **Coverage:** Add installed-javaagent regressions for simple and direct containers across baseline/latest dependencies, including partial delivery failure and misleading count headers.
metadata.title: Fix Spring Rabbit producer-batch message undercounting
